summary: Ivan Stchoukine was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Between circa 1920 and 1928, he studied under Paul Pelliot and Alfred Foucher.

Ivanna Otroshchenko specializes in Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. She earned her Magister at Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv (1989–1994) and served as a Leading Research Fellow at the A. Yu. Krymskyi Institute of Oriental Studies in 1998.

Ivar Ulrik Wallenius worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Katedralskolan i Åbo and the Royal Academy of Turku (M.A. 1811–1815), he became Docent of Arabic at Turku (1817) and Associate Professor of Oriental Literature at the University of Helsinki (1824–1852).

Linguist Ives Goddard studied at Harvard College (1959–1963) and Harvard University (circa 1963–1969). He held posts at Harvard University (~1966–1976), the Smithsonian Institution (~1976–2025), and the National Museum of Natural History (~1976–2025).
Ives Waldo works in philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Oxford and studied under Chögyam Trungpa from 1970 to 1988.

Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University by 2003, studying under Leonard van der Kuijp, Charles Hallisey, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and held a fellowship post at Grinnell College.

Ivo Fišer worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Vincenc Lesný and Oldřich Friš, earning his doctorate by 1953, and held positions at Charles University (attested 1960) and the University of Copenhagen (attested 1970).

Iwao Ishikawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. His appointments include research positions at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2000, 2026) and lectureships at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Iwao Nakajima works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Hitotsubashi University and under Nichiki Kimura, and held positions at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and at Sandhaan (attested 1999).

Iwao Shima worked in Indology and philosophy. After studying at Nagoya University from circa 1969 to 1977, he held academic positions at Kanazawa University from circa 1988 to 2007, serving as professor from circa 2000 to 2007.

Izumi Hoshi specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. She completed her undergraduate and graduate education at the University of Tokyo between circa 1987 and 1997, later serving at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies as Assistant Professor (1997) and director (2019–2023).
Izumi Matsuda-Kiami specializes in Japanology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and serves as Teaching Professor at the University of Washington (attested 2026).

Indologist and philosopher J. A. B. van Buitenen earned his PhD under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University (1946–1953). He held posts at Deccan College (1953–1956), Utrecht University (1959–1961), and the University of Chicago (1957–1959; 1961–1964).

J. A. F. Roodbergen was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Adriaan Scharpé and founded the India Institute, Amsterdam. He served as associate professor at the University of Amsterdam from circa 1968 to 1990.
J. B. Disanayaka is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held a professorship at the University of Colombo from circa 1982 to 2002 and held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 1996).

J. C. Wright worked in Indology and linguistics, serving as Professor of Sanskrit at SOAS University of London and Professor at the University of London. Wright also earned an MD at the University of London (2007) and worked at Hamlin Fistula International (2013).

J. Daniel White is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He was affiliated with the Library of Congress (attested 1994) and served as Professor of Indian Studies at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte (attested 2000–2001).

Indologist J. Duncan M. Derrett was educated at Emanuel School, Jesus College, Oxford (~1940–1947), and SOAS University of London (~1947–1949). He served on the faculty of the University of London from circa 1951 to 1982.

J. F. Blakiston was a specialist in history, archaeology, and Indology educated at Wellington College (~1896–1900). He worked at the Archaeological Survey of India as assistant (1911), Superintendent (1916), and Director-General (1935–1937).

J. G. Jennings worked in Indology and Buddhist studies after earning an M.A. from the University of Oxford (~1885–1889). He served as teacher of English (1898) and Principal (1906–1913) at Muir Central College, and Director of Public Instruction for Bihar and Orissa (~1917–1921).
